builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
summary: AST replaces fixed-codebook residual or hierarchical vector quantization (e.g., RQ-VAE) for semantic ID construction with a top-down divisive clustering tree whose branching factor is chosen per node by maximizing the silhouette coefficient, plus constrained variants enforcing minimum probability mass for long-tail items. Cost is limited to an offline clustering pass over item embeddings and retraining the generative recommender on the new IDs, which fits a single 24 GB GPU; no serving-time overhead is added. Failure modes include dependence on the quality of the input item embeddings, sensitivity of silhouette-based splitting to dataset density structure, and unverified benefit outside Amazon Review-style domains given the absence of quantified results in the abstract.
rationale: The method is an inexpensive offline preprocessing step compatible with constrained infrastructure, but its unquantified quality gains and domain specificity require validation on the reader's own recommendation workload before production adoption.
technique: Adaptive tree-based semantic ID construction for recommenders
